name: SolidFrame
lead: Build and edit native mechanical solids in a browser, with a complete CAD workspace rather than a static model viewer.
problem: A useful browser CAD tool needs editable geometry, reversible changes and portable documents. A rendered mesh alone cannot carry the dimensions that produced a part.
mechanism: SolidFrame builds on Chili3D and OpenCascade. The mechanical-part workflow turns dimensions and hole layouts into native solids, while the editable fixture exposes separate parts in the model tree. Properties edits rebuild geometry; the command history makes changes reversible. Local browser snapshots and editable .cd downloads serve different storage needs.
observed_result: In the recorded deployed workflow, Open editable sample created seven native solids. Editing the selected base plate changed Width from 70 to 85 mm. Undo returned it to 70 mm; Redo restored 85 mm, with all seven parts retained.
scope_note: The fixture contains independent editable solids, not a constraint-solved assembly or a manufacturing-approved design. This capture verifies the shown edit and history sequence, not every CAD command or export format.
foundations: Adapted from Chili3D and built on OpenCascade. The AGPL-3.0 source license and the C++/WebAssembly notice remain with the project and the retained case assets.

media.alt: SolidFrame with the seven-part workholding fixture, the base plate selected and its Width property set to 85 millimetres.

technical_details: Native .cd documents preserve editable project structure. Exchange exports such as STEP and STL carry geometry; they do not promise to preserve all builder settings.
The project includes a drilled-plate and bracket builder with whole-configuration validation. Its ideal geometry does not calculate strength, bend allowance or fabrication approval.

name: Capsulith
lead: Run a prepared native image component in the browser, reopen its initialized pixel allocation in a fresh worker, and inspect the result.
problem: A native component can depend on initialized state and owned memory, not just a function address. Reusing it requires preserving that state and an explicit calling contract.
mechanism: Capsulith packages selected ARM64 functions with calling contracts and owned memory. The image workbench runs the prepared QOI decoder through native-code emulation, retains the decoded allocation, then reopens it in a fresh worker. Pixel inspection and native free expose the memory lifecycle instead of hiding it behind a static preview.
observed_result: The November 16 browser run reported that 49,152 restored RGBA bytes matched the prior native output and that native free completed. Pixel (64, 48) read RGBA (126, 135, 250, 255).
scope_note: This is one observed prepared Orbit example. The workbench comparison is not an independent native oracle, a new codec, universal binary compatibility or a security-isolation proof. The exact source revision of this retained screenshot was not recorded.
foundations: QOI is by Dominic Szablewski and contributors under MIT. Native emulation uses Unicorn.js and Unicorn. Capsulith’s runtime is GPL-2.0-only; the project retains the complete third-party notices.

media.alt: Actual Capsulith image workbench after decoding the prepared Orbit QOI image and restoring its native pixels in a fresh worker.
media.caption: Actual browser capture, November 16, 2026. The prepared decoder output was reopened, its 49,152 RGBA bytes compared, and the native allocation freed.

name: QLOOM
lead: Compile a logical quantum circuit for a device graph, inspect the physical operations and mapping, and check that its meaning survives.
problem: A physical circuit must respect a device’s connectivity without silently changing the logical program. Gate count alone cannot show whether routing, placement and phase have been handled correctly.
mechanism: QLOOM searches a bounded set of compiler strategies on a CPU. The Studio exposes the logical input, physical gates, logical-to-physical mapping, candidate costs and numerical verification. A trained policy ranks strategies, while explicit checks decide whether a candidate preserves the supported program’s meaning.
observed_result: The retained three-qubit line-device example maps H(q0), CX(q0,q2) and Ry(0.31)(q1) to selected physical operations U(p1), U(p2) and CX(p1,p0). Initial and final mappings are [1, 2, 0]. The recorded maximum operator error is 1.401642967028923e-16 against tolerance 1e-8.
scope_note: This is one stored synthetic example with a two-candidate budget. No SWAP appears in this selected circuit. Numerical evidence is not a formal equivalence proof, a QPU execution or a claim that the learned policy beats established compilers.
foundations: Qiskit supplies circuit interchange and standard gate translation. QLOOM implements the selected layout/routing strategies; Qiskit levels, MQT QMAP and BQSKit are separately attributed comparison tools with their own licenses.

media.alt: Recorded QLOOM logical gates beside selected physical operations and the logical-to-physical mapping for the synthetic three-qubit line device.
media.caption: Presentation of the retained line-3 report. Exact angles and terminal measurements remain in the source record; the compact drawing omits the terminal measurement symbols.

technical_details: The diagram reads the saved report rather than running a new compiler experiment. It must not be confused with the separate five-qubit, eight-candidate Studio demonstration.

The project’s measured study retains ties, failures and timeouts. It does not establish broad learned-policy superiority; the complete comparison belongs with its stated budgets and verification results.

name: PhotonSmith
lead: Design a periodic photonic grating, inspect its solved electric field and spectrum, and compare the result with a separate numerical formulation.
problem: An optimizer can find geometry that looks promising to a learned model while failing a physical solve or a stronger numerical check. The design needs a trace from target and geometry to field, power and validation.
mechanism: PhotonSmith searches a constrained three-layer periodic grating. A compact learned surrogate screens candidates, a Fourier-modal Maxwell solver and adjoint refinement evaluate them, and a separately assembled real-space solver checks the result. The Studio keeps the target, geometry, field, spectrum and exported evidence together.
observed_result: For the retained refined 1550 nm design, the stored M9 target-order efficiency is 0.9358787717897128, about 93.59% of incident power into order +1. M13 and independent real-space checks are separately recorded. The figure pairs the same design’s field with all 21 stored wavelength solves.
scope_note: This is a two-dimensional periodic numerical model, not a fabricated-device measurement. Agreement between the disclosed resolutions and formulations does not certify convergence, omitted physics, global optimality or manufacturing readiness.
foundations: The runtime uses NumPy and SciPy. Research foundations and optional external validation tools are separately credited in the repository; an available Meep adapter is not evidence of an executed Meep validation.

media.alt: Stored PhotonSmith real electric field across one grating cell and target-order efficiency across the retained wavelength samples.
media.caption: The retained 1550 nm refined design: Re(Ey), relative to unit incident amplitude, and 21 sampled wavelength solves. This is a stored M9 simulation, not intensity or device data.

technical_details: The field figure uses all 97 × 96 stored real-field values at equal spatial x/z scale. It does not smooth, normalize or replace the stored numerical arrays with an illustration.
Search used M5; the displayed final solve uses M9, with M13 and independent-grid results recorded separately. The spectrum lines connect actual samples without adding intermediate solutions.

name: VibeScope
lead: Measure small motion from original video frames, then change the display gain without changing the displacement history or frequency estimate.
problem: A convincing magnified video is not a displacement measurement. Display enhancement must remain separate from the original-frame signal used for quantitative analysis.
mechanism: VibeScope tracks a selected image region against an independent stationary reference, derives displacement and frequency information from original decoded frames, and renders motion visualization separately. Exported reports, CSV and saved-run history retain the settings and measurement records.
observed_result: The recorded gain-5 and gain-20 runs have identical complete 240-sample signals, quantitative metrics and raw displacement CSV bytes, while their visualization settings and enhanced output differ. For the controlled 7.3 Hz / 0.28 px input, the observed result was 7.299959660082684 Hz / 0.2798920570385787 px. The saved gain-20 run reopened after server restart.
scope_note: This is controlled synthetic image-plane evidence. Physical calibration, arbitrary-media and diagnostic accuracy are not established. Timing was explicitly unverified because ffprobe was unavailable; magnification is a visualization, not a new sensor measurement.
foundations: Core inference runs in NumPy. The project separately credits its classical and learned research foundations; the optional EulerMormer runner invokes an external model and is not bundled into the core estimator.

media.alt: Actual original and gain-20 enhanced frames, followed by the identical gain-5 and gain-20 displacement traces and a spectrum from the original frames.
media.caption: Recorded synthetic paired runs. Frame 72 shows original input and gain-20 visualization; all 240 displacement samples per gain and 120 positive-frequency bins are retained in the figure and source artifacts.

media.alt: Actual VibeScope workspace after reopening the saved gain-20 measurement following a server restart.
media.caption: The recorded workspace reopened the saved gain-20 run after server restart. The source video, completed result and warnings remain part of the measurement history.

technical_details: The original and enhanced frame pixels are retained at native 320 × 192 resolution; nearest-neighbor enlargement changes display size only. No selective contrast, color or denoising adjustment was applied for the portfolio figure.
The figure reads the browser-exported reports and CSVs. It performs no new estimator, fit, filter or physical experiment.

name: InstrumentZero
lead: Create a seeded ringdown, compare processing placements, and inspect the resonance and damping estimates alongside the signal and its assumptions.
problem: A frequency or damping estimate is hard to assess without the input signal, processing path and calibration assumptions. Agreement with a reference calculation also needs to be distinguished from a physical measurement.
mechanism: InstrumentZero turns supported experiment questions into procedures, calibration contracts and executable analysis. This case uses its Edge simulation workflow: a seeded signal passes through explicit processing placements, with sample records and numerical references retained beside the estimates.
observed_result: The retained custom ringdown contains 769 displayed acceleration samples. Its analytic model is 9.75 Hz with decay 0.45 s⁻¹ at seed 9132301. The stored numerical reference returns 9.750006565906396 Hz and decay 0.4499236618270089 s⁻¹ on the same captured input.
scope_note: This is seeded simulation and a same-input numerical reference, not a physical sensor capture or independently measured resonance. The declared resolution/clock envelope is not a validated confidence interval or a coverage guarantee.
foundations: The retained reference uses NumPy float64 processing and SciPy lfilter, distinguished from the recorded C-path results. The project’s external recordings and dependencies retain their own notices; none is relabeled as this synthetic capture.

media.alt: All stored acceleration samples of the seeded InstrumentZero ringdown with its retained reference frequency and decay.
media.caption: Seeded 9.75 Hz, 0.45 s⁻¹ ringdown. All 769 stored plot samples are shown without new fitting or filtering; the eight-second run’s processed plot segment ends at 7.68 seconds.

technical_details: The portfolio figure displays stored time in seconds and acceleration in m/s². Connecting lines aid reading between samples and do not create additional observations.

The same retained JSON includes raw-host, calibrated-edge and filtered-edge C-path results, estimator diagnostics and source identity. It supports comparing processing paths without calling numerical agreement a hardware measurement.

name: nstack
lead: Find a reviewed specialist capability, inspect its exact source and prerequisites, then decide whether it belongs in the current task.
problem: A list of agent skills does not explain when a capability applies, what it depends on or which licensed source will be installed. Discovery needs to stay separate from activation.
mechanism: nstack keeps a reviewed capability registry with source revisions, selected paths, rights, activation conditions and task checks. Its search, show and route commands expose those decisions before installation. A component can contain several native skills; its catalog identifier is not the same as an installed skill name.
observed_result: The recorded search for web-ui-design returned component L010 with web-ui-design and mcp-builder. Show and route exposed the pinned upstream source, selected paths, rights and prerequisites. The absent temporary state directory stayed absent throughout this read-only session.
scope_note: This case verifies source-only discovery, not an installed runtime, live activation, rollback or another machine’s setup. A catalog route is not permission to install, and available source is not target-specific acceptance.
foundations: Each selected capability keeps its upstream identity and license. In this recorded L010 case, the source is anthropics/skills at ca45fc496a3436251f191354091d557da31c15b5; only the eligible selected leaves are covered by the stated route.
technical_details: The actual command sequence is python3 nstack.py search web-ui-design --brief, followed by show L010 and route L010. The complete JSON outputs are retained as site assets, so readers can inspect the result rather than a mock terminal.
The selected route distinguishes Apache-2.0 frontend/MCP leaves from restricted artifact sources. Discovery, source preparation and actual target-runtime checks remain separate operations.

name: Solidrift
lead: Shrink a native mesh Boolean failure while preserving the bug, then inspect a reversible geometry intervention and its source ancestry.
problem: A Boolean union quietly drops part of the input. Sending the full model is easy; reducing it to a valid, small example that still reproduces the same failure is harder.
mechanism: Solidrift contracts edges while checking that both operands remain valid closed solids and the same native failure survives. It tracks each vertex’s source ancestry, searches small boundary interventions on the witness, lifts a selected intervention back to the full inputs, and records native repair and undo results.
observed_result: The retained investigation reduces 132 input triangles to a 12-triangle witness through 60 accepted contractions. Its recorded intervention moves three witness vertices whose ancestry covers thirteen original vertices. Undo restores the original input coordinates and the native omission. The two portfolio panels show the original 132-triangle stage, not the later witness.
scope_note: The browser viewer replays stored geometry and never runs Blender. This is a bounded greedy reduction, not a globally smallest witness. The intervention changes the input geometry, not Blender’s implementation; agreement with MANIFOLD is not proof of an ideal union.
foundations: The two operands are Manifold regression fixtures under Apache-2.0, not original models. Blender supplies the FLOAT and MANIFOLD Boolean implementations. Solidrift’s implementation is MIT licensed, with fixture attribution retained.

media.alt: The original recorded Solidrift input: two overlapping mesh bodies, one cyan and one blue, before the FLOAT union.
media.caption: Original 132-triangle input stage, recomposed from preserved polygon coordinates. These are Manifold regression fixtures.

media.alt: The recorded Blender FLOAT union retains the blue body while the cyan body is absent.
media.caption: Stored FLOAT output for the original inputs. The figure is a recorded result, not a fresh Blender execution or an image of the 12-triangle witness.

technical_details: This case is tied to the retained Blender 5.3.0 Alpha build bad8871dc58d record at the cited source revision. Newer public investigations have separate backend identities and must not be merged into this older capture’s provenance.

The compact case bundles original identities, reduced and restored operands, contraction trace, coordinate patch, validity checks and backend identity. Intermediate input states can be replayed without inventing intermediate native output surfaces.

name: MaterialMind
lead: Compare crystal stability predictions and active-learning query choices with archived computed reference data.

secondary_action.label: Inspect and reopen the recorded case

problem: A high query rank or confident stability score can hide an inaccurate energy prediction. The evidence needs to distinguish what the model knew before reveal from the archived reference it is compared against.
mechanism: The workbench retains an initial crystal, its pre-reveal prediction and uncertainty, and the acquisition components used to choose a query. Revealing the existing DFT reference exposes that one selected energy lies outside the stated interval; it does not acquire a new physical measurement.
observed_result: PaMnF6 ranks first in this recorded query. Its pre-reveal energy estimate is −2.198549726666667 eV/atom, with a stated 90% interval from −2.284320417627142 to −2.1127790357061924. The archived reference is −1.951794 eV/atom, outside that interval. Both energies are below the fixed reference hull.
scope_note: One selected retrospective interval miss, not an uncertainty-coverage study or new DFT calculation. The fitted policy did not outperform adapted greedy in the released study. No synthesis, physical stability or official blind-benchmark claim.
foundations: Retained WBM/Matbench Discovery computed reference data, Janosh Riebesell and contributors, CC-BY-4.0; original WBM by Wang, Botti and Marques. Code MIT. Original data attribution and transformations stay with the case assets.

media.alt: PaMnF6 initial crystal, pre-reveal model interval and archived DFT energy outside that interval; the query score explains why the model ranked it first.
media.caption: Unchanged source-derived figure from the recorded initial crystal, pre-reveal prediction and revealed computed reference. A selected failure of the interval, not a new coverage study.

technical_details: The crystal view uses the retained lattice and eight atomic sites. It does not represent a synthesized specimen or predict a new structure.

Query rank, stability probability and energy-interval accuracy answer different questions. The source, raw values, native save/reopen evidence and negative aggregate result remain available in the owning repository.

name: SILICONPILOT
lead: Turn a small neural classifier into inspectable hardware, then see what accuracy, area and latency cost.
problem: A neural model is only the start of a hardware design. Precision, multiplier reuse and scheduling change its answers, circuit size and speed. Those choices need visible arithmetic, generated hardware and comparable implementation evidence.
mechanism: SILICONPILOT compiles fixed-shape dense/ReLU networks into signed fixed-point Verilog. An independent integer reference checks output bits and handshakes in RTL simulation; an open ECP5 synthesis and routing flow records implementation costs. The observatory connects each saved design to its source, waveform, resource report and tradeoff position.
observed_result: The recorded corpus contains 40 RTL-verified, synthesized and routed designs. In the demonstrated constraint change, a 1,929-LUT4 design has 0.52 microseconds of simulated core latency; a 1,170-LUT4 alternative has 2.00 microseconds. Both retain 100% accuracy on this validation split. A separate LUT-only mapped implementation matches the integer reference on 353 vectors.
scope_note: These are recorded simulations and FPGA-tool estimates, not board measurements. The pictured 0.1.0 corpus is preserved separately from the newer 0.1.1.dev0 compiler.
foundations: Original small RTL backend using established ML-to-FPGA and surrogate-search ideas. Icarus Verilog, Yosys and nextpnr supply simulation, synthesis and routing. Four precomputed input features come from Volker Lohweg’s UCI Banknote Authentication dataset (CC BY 4.0), not raw camera frames. Source is Apache-2.0; retain its license and upstream dataset/tool notices.

media.alt: Recorded SILICONPILOT observatory with selected design w8-c16 and its generated fixed-point Verilog.
media.caption: Recorded 0.1.0 design w8-c16: generated HDL, 1,929 mapped LUT4 equivalents and 0.52 microseconds simulated packed-core latency. The 33.6 MHz value is a routing-tool estimate, not a measured board clock.

media.alt: Recorded waveform replay associated with a selected compiled SILICONPILOT design.
media.caption: Saved waveform evidence from the original 0.1.0 corpus: recorded RTL simulation, not a live compile or physical logic-analyzer trace.

technical_details: The recorded case source pin is v0.1.0 at 61badd38086dc8c0395fff3dfd814f4073c90b93. Current source 6e2bbbe2faca1f10eb4a2a1e71a8aa858c56ffd1 identifies itself as 0.1.1.dev0. The online observatory is a static evidence browser; the separate local compiler action produces new RTL.

The current overlapped-products-v2 schedule reports 49 clocks to core output availability and a 34-clock sustained interval for the default packaged 4→8→2 model; two lanes with product pipelining report 27 and 19. These current modeled/simulation-checked values are not historical screenshot implementation costs. Recompiling an old configuration requires fresh synthesis and routing.

Core cycle latency excludes serial-shell transfers, stalls and board I/O. Fmax is a nextpnr estimate for the disclosed ECP5 device/constraint; pins are automatically assigned and external I/O delays unspecified. No physical FPGA was tested. Default DSP-mapped designs have a documented simulation-model limitation; the separate LUT-only mapped-netlist result does not validate every mapping.

Host preprocessing supplies four standardized wavelet features. Search uses validation rows; 100% validation is not test-population robustness or a deployed authentication result. UCI data attribution is Volker Lohweg, DOI 10.24432/C55P57, CC BY 4.0; the original source/provenance and changes remain documented.

The matched-budget finite replay does not show broad learned-search superiority: the fixed sweep recovers the full reference tradeoff volume and uses less compilation time on average. Cost uncertainty under-covers. Established compilers/search methods, including hls4ml, are credited in docs/research.md; this project does not invent hardware-aware optimization.

name: MorphProof
lead: Find the input where a Python-to-Rust transformation changes the answer, then keep a replayable witness.
problem: A successful build does not show that rewritten code behaves the same way. A useful transformation workflow needs an explicit input contract, observable comparisons and a small case that explains any disagreement.
mechanism: MorphProof compiles a bounded numerical Python subset into a Rust-backed package. Separate workers run reference and candidate under the declared contract; bounded minimization reduces a mismatch to a replayable input. The portable Studio puts source, tested inputs, observed differences and untested claims together, while the worked artifact retains native snapshots and notices.
observed_result: In the disclosed synthetic example, a deliberately inserted loop omission reduces [1.0, -1.0] to the witness [1.0]: Python returns 1.0 and Rust returns 0.0. Restoring the generated loop passes 64 fresh positional comparisons and 3 keyword checks. The native worked package reopens in a fresh Python 3.12 environment; newer native CI separately builds and imports packages on Linux, macOS ARM64 and Windows.
scope_note: The loop omission is a disclosed seed and its restoration is deterministic. Finite comparisons do not prove universal equivalence; the portable Studio replays evidence rather than executing uploaded code.
foundations: Original MIT-licensed compiler, comparison workflow and evidence viewer, using Python, Rust, PyO3 0.27.2 and Maturin. Keep the worked artifact’s MIT license, dependency manifest and actual Cargo dependency notices. Separately attributed upstream experiment fixtures remain distinct from this one-function example.

media.alt: Actual MorphProof Studio showing generated Rust, behavioral claims and the minimized input whose Python and Rust results differ.
media.caption: Current Studio capture at 36208c6 exposes source, the disclosed failure and explicitly untested claims. It reads recorded evidence; it does not run a transformation in the browser.

media.alt: Mechanism diagram of a disclosed skip-first-item seed: input [1.0] returns Python 1.0 and Rust 0.0; deterministic restoration passes the finite comparisons.
media.caption: Diagram from the actual native record, not a performance chart. That record used Rust 1.100.0; its footer’s unexercised 1.99.1 statement is historical. Later separate CI exercised 1.99.1 on three operating systems.

technical_details: Current Studio/public source is 36208c6a6ed15ae62c62e73eb99076fd5c79286d. The original one-function native run used source 80a0daaf3eec332642159971ac33b8c59e3d0eaf, Rust/cargo 1.100.0, PyO3 0.27.2 and Python 3.12.13. The diagram first appeared at 399600c51eba4b14821f65517a8388f66495cbf9 and remains unchanged. Do not relabel its binary as a Rust 1.99.1 artifact.

Later current-source CI exercised Rust/cargo 1.99.1 on Linux, macOS ARM64 and Windows, including transformation, wheel build, installation and keyword import. This is separate evidence from the original witness, not a repeat of every historical timing or selector experiment.

The supported subset is pure deterministic numerical functions with one list[float] argument and float result. It handles declared keyword names, binary64 operation order, signed zero, infinity and NaN class as documented. Arbitrary repositories, NumPy objects and stateful code are outside the claim; unsupported syntax is refused.

Five bounded minimization calls found [1.0], not a proven globally smallest witness. Comparison budgets are not unique-input counts: each positional campaign contains 27 unique inputs. Passing the restored campaign is finite evidence, not autonomous repair or formal proof.

The Studio is a portable recorded evidence viewer. Exact retained native snapshots require macOS ARM64 and Python 3.12; other systems rebuild with an explicit toolchain. Its abi3 wheel tag does not establish every platform/interpreter combination. Worker separation isolates state/time, not filesystem access: execute trusted source only.

If redistributing native artifacts, preserve docs/presentation/LICENSE.txt, DEPENDENCIES.md, Cargo.lock files and the actual dependency notices. This portfolio links the intact worked package rather than stripping notices or copying its binaries. Separately attributed boltons/more_itertools research fixtures are not inputs to this case.

name: LadderProof
lead: Find when a higher digital code produces a lower voltage, then choose resistor tolerances that prevent it.
problem: A digital-to-analog converter should increase its output as the input code increases. Resistor variation can reverse a step. Knowing the worst allowed step and which tolerances repair it turns a bad example into a design decision.
mechanism: LadderProof enumerates every admitted corner of a small resistor-tolerance box using exact fractions. A nodal circuit solve finds the worst adjacent-code transition and attaining resistor assignment; a separate Thevenin-based verifier recomputes the complete bounds. A finite catalog search trades user-defined component costs against a required minimum step.
observed_result: The included six-bit ±5% case decreases at code 31→32, while the ±1% case has no decreasing step across all 4,096 modeled corners. In the synthetic two-bit catalog, tightening B1 and S0 meets the 1/5 V requirement for cost 2 rather than cost 4 for every part. The chosen exact worst step is 151/731 V; the all-loose baseline is 68/409 V.
scope_note: Exact results apply to the declared ideal static 2–6-bit circuit and independent resistor intervals. Catalog costs are synthetic units, not part prices; this is not measured hardware or manufacturing yield.
foundations: Established R–2R circuit analysis and exact arithmetic, implemented as an inspectable bounded analyzer with a separate complete verifier. The project credits its model references and keeps its MIT license. It is not a SPICE replacement or an invention of the converter architecture.

media.alt: Six-bit resistor-ladder analysis with a negative 31 to 32 voltage step and the exact attaining resistor assignment.
media.caption: Retained ideal six-bit ±5% example: the 31→32 step is −269227/7660721 V at a 1 V reference. The component assignment and complete interval result are inspectable; no physical voltage was measured.

mobile_details.alt: Recorded negative minimum step and the 31 to 32 transition.

media.alt: LadderProof finite-catalog result for the synthetic two-bit example, cost 2 and independently verified selected tolerances.
media.caption: Actual finite-catalog workflow published at 12604d1: cost 2 synthetic units and exact minimum step 151/731 V. A limited search reports unfinished rather than claiming optimality.

technical_details: This case is pinned to the complete finite-catalog workflow at 12604d131498ba3851bea6a45066a0d1d71fa7c0, corresponding to actual approved V6 computation. Later ccb0d22ad1651390ae86283143f8b069bd7dc78b is a CSS-only V7 successor: narrow labels/focus were checked while JS, HTML and exact arithmetic stayed unchanged. This is not a new V7 worker computation run.

The retained workbench image originated at 67925bd3140d004164248f119aafcebd943644dd and remains unchanged in this workflow. Its exact minimum is −269227/7660721 V; the ±1% minimum is 186147971/34016602567 V. Verification re-enumerates every corner, not merely the displayed adverse assignment.

The recorded browser workflow exercised optimal selection, finite exhaustion/infeasibility, a work-limit stop, malformed exact-fraction recovery and independent Verify and use selection. The successful two-bit selection was independently recomputed over 16 corners and 3 adjacent transitions.

The model assumes ideal switches, a fixed positive reference and unloaded output. Independent intervals do not model matched/correlated resistor families. Switching glitches, settling, temperature, noise, reference regulation and physical yield are outside the result.

Search returns optimal only under its exact cost-order/verification conditions, infeasible after exhausting the admitted finite catalog, and unfinished when candidate/corner/deadline limits stop it. Arbitrary additive costs are not prices. Certificates are replayable computations, not succinct formal proofs or cryptographic attestations.

Keep the MIT license and docs/references.md context with redistributed material. Runtime uses Python standard-library exact arithmetic and local browser code; no account, paid service or hardware is needed.
